items.question: Complete using the British English past-tense form of smell (five letters): Yesterday she ___ smoke.
items.specific_reason: smelt is a British English past tense of smell; five letters and explicitly British framing distinguish smelled. Sentence is grammatical; rare-form focus is explicit.
items.suggested_fix: Optional learner note: smelled is also widely used; avoid presenting smelt as the sole past form globally.

items.question: Use the past tense of hang meaning remain suspended: The curtains ___ loosely from the rod.
items.specific_reason: The meaning 'remain suspended' and past tense cue unambiguously select hung rather than execution-related hanged. Natural sentence.

items.question: Use the regular past-tense form of wet ending in -ted: She ___ the sponge before cleaning.
items.specific_reason: Both wet and wetted can function as past tense; explicit regular-form and -ted constraints correctly narrow the accepted response to wetted. Sentence is natural.
items.suggested_fix: Optional learner note: wet also occurs as past tense; use constraints only for morphology exercises.
